topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, the Act defines a "managing broker" as a licensee who:
choice_a: may be authorized to assume responsibilities as a designated managing broker for licensees in one or, in a multi-office company, more than one office, upon appointment by the sponsoring broker and registration with the Department
choice_b: automatically supervises every licensee in the State once licensed
choice_c: is appointed solely by the Department without sponsoring broker involvement
choice_d: must hold an ownership interest in the sponsoring brokerage
explanation: Section 1-10 defines "managing broker" as a licensee who may be authorized to assume designated-managing-broker responsibilities for one or more offices upon appointment by the sponsoring broker and registration with the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, a managing broker may act as:
choice_a: one's own sponsor
choice_b: a sponsor only for residential leasing agents
choice_c: a sponsor only if co-designated with another managing broker
choice_d: a sponsor solely for corporations, never individuals
explanation: The "managing broker" definition in Section 1-10 specifically notes that a managing broker may act as one's own sponsor.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, the Act defines "office" as:
choice_a: a broker's place of business where the general public is invited to transact business and where records may be maintained and licenses readily available, whether or not it is the broker's principal place of business
choice_b: only the sponsoring broker's principal place of business
choice_c: any location where a licensee happens to meet a client
choice_d: a location registered with the county recorder
explanation: Section 1-10 defines "office" broadly as a broker's place of business where the public is invited to transact business and records/licenses are kept, regardless of whether it is the principal place of business.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, when describing the relationship between a sponsoring broker and a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent, the term "employee" is construed to include:
choice_a: an independent contractor relationship, provided that a written agreement exists that clearly establishes and states the relationship
choice_b: only individuals on the sponsoring broker's payroll
choice_c: any unlicensed assistant performing clerical tasks
choice_d: only relationships lasting more than one year
explanation: Section 1-10 provides that "employee" is construed to include an independent contractor relationship, so long as a written agreement clearly establishes and states that relationship.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, a "team" of licensees must, among other requirements, be:
choice_a: supervised by the same managing broker and sponsored by the same sponsoring broker
choice_b: registered with the Department as a distinct licensed business entity
choice_c: composed of at least five licensees
choice_d: led by a licensee with at least ten years of experience
explanation: Section 1-10 defines a "team" as licensees who, among other criteria, are together supervised by the same managing broker and sponsored by the same sponsoring broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, a "team," as defined by the Act:
choice_a: does not mean a separately organized, incorporated, or legal entity
choice_b: must be incorporated separately from the sponsoring broker
choice_c: is automatically treated as a limited liability company
choice_d: requires its own Department license distinct from its members' licenses
explanation: Section 1-10 clarifies that a "team" does not mean a separately organized, incorporated, or legal entity, even though its members share a team name and identity.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, a "sponsoring broker" is defined as the broker who:
choice_a: certifies to the Department the broker's sponsorship of a licensed managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent
choice_b: owns the largest share of the brokerage entity
choice_c: has held a license the longest among the firm's brokers
choice_d: is designated by majority vote of the office's licensees
explanation: Section 1-10 defines "sponsoring broker" as the broker who certifies to the Department the broker's sponsorship of a licensed managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, all brokerage agreements shall be:
choice_a: in writing, and may be exclusive or non-exclusive
choice_b: oral unless the client requests a written copy
choice_c: valid only if notarized
choice_d: limited to a maximum term of 90 days
explanation: Section 1-10's "brokerage agreement" definition requires all brokerage agreements to be in writing, and states that they may be exclusive or non-exclusive.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 1-10, the license of a business entity that is not in good standing with the Illinois Secretary of State, or is not authorized to conduct business in Illinois:
choice_a: shall immediately become inactive, and the entity is prohibited from engaging in any licensed activities
choice_b: remains fully active until the next renewal period
choice_c: is automatically revoked with no right to reinstatement
choice_d: is suspended only if the Department separately initiates discipline
explanation: Section 1-10's "Inactive" definition provides that a business entity not in good standing with, or not authorized to do business by, the Secretary of State immediately becomes inactive and may not engage in licensed activities.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(a), a valid sponsorship must be registered with the Department:
choice_a: either directly or through the Department's authorized designee
choice_b: only directly, with no designee permitted
choice_c: only through the licensee's local county clerk
choice_d: only after the licensee's first renewal period
explanation: Section 5-15(a) requires a license and a valid sponsorship registered with the Department, either directly or through its authorized designee.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(b), besides every actively participating officer, who else must hold a license as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent in a licensed corporation?
choice_a: Every employee who acts as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent for the corporation
choice_b: Only employees who have worked at the corporation for over one year
choice_c: No employees, only officers, need be licensed
choice_d: Only the corporation's registered agent
explanation: Section 5-15(b) requires every employee who acts as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent for the corporation to hold the appropriate license, in addition to actively participating officers.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(b), a corporation may not be granted a license if:
choice_a: any nonparticipating owner or officer has previously been publicly disciplined by the Department resulting in that licensee being currently barred from real estate practice because of a suspension or revocation
choice_b: the corporation has fewer than three officers
choice_c: the corporation was formed less than one year ago
choice_d: any officer has ever changed sponsoring brokers
explanation: Section 5-15(b) bars licensure of a corporation if any nonparticipating owner or officer was previously publicly disciplined by the Department and is currently barred from practice due to suspension or revocation.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(c), apart from the specific rule for registered limited liability partnerships, a general partnership may not be granted a broker license unless:
choice_a: every partner in the partnership who actively participates in the partnership's real estate activities holds a license as a managing broker or broker
choice_b: at least one partner has held a license for 10 years
choice_c: the partnership has a written buy-sell agreement
choice_d: every partner, participating or not, is individually bonded
explanation: Section 5-15(c) requires every partner in a general partnership who actively participates in the partnership's real estate activities to hold a license as a managing broker or broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(c), what must nonparticipating partners of a licensed partnership submit to the Department?
choice_a: Affidavits of nonparticipation as required by the Department
choice_b: A certified copy of the partnership agreement
choice_c: A surety bond covering the partnership's escrow accounts
choice_d: Proof of errors and omissions insurance
explanation: Section 5-15(c) requires all nonparticipating partners to submit affidavits of nonparticipation as required by the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(c), a partnership may not be granted a license if:
choice_a: any nonparticipating partner has previously been publicly disciplined by the Department resulting in that licensee being currently barred from real estate practice because of a suspension or revocation
choice_b: the partnership has more than 10 partners
choice_c: the partnership was dissolved and later reformed
choice_d: any partner resides outside of Illinois
explanation: Section 5-15(c) bars licensure of a partnership if any nonparticipating partner was previously publicly disciplined by the Department and is currently barred from practice due to suspension or revocation.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(d), besides every actively participating member or manager, who else in a limited liability company must hold a license as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent?
choice_a: Every other member and employee who acts as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent for the limited liability company
choice_b: Only members holding more than a 25% ownership interest
choice_c: No one else; only actively participating members and managers need be licensed
choice_d: Only the LLC's registered agent
explanation: Section 5-15(d) also requires every other member and employee who acts as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent for the LLC to hold the appropriate license.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(d), a limited liability company may not be granted a license if:
choice_a: any nonparticipating member or manager has previously been publicly disciplined by the Department resulting in that licensee being currently barred from real estate practice because of a suspension or revocation
choice_b: the LLC's operating agreement has not been notarized
choice_c: the LLC has converted from a corporation within the past year
choice_d: any manager also serves on a homeowners association board
explanation: Section 5-15(d) bars licensure of an LLC if any nonparticipating member or manager was previously publicly disciplined by the Department and is currently barred from practice due to suspension or revocation.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(a), in each office of a sponsoring broker who maintains more than one office within the State, what must be displayed?
choice_a: The brokerage license, conspicuously
choice_b: A copy of the Real Estate License Act of 2000 in its entirety
choice_c: The Department's toll-free complaint hotline number only
choice_d: A list of all licensees who have ever worked at the office
explanation: Section 5-45(a) requires the brokerage license to be displayed conspicuously in each office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(b), apart from later reporting any changes, what must a sponsoring broker initially notify the Department of regarding designated managing brokers?
choice_a: The name of all designated managing brokers of the sponsoring broker and the office or offices they manage
choice_b: Only the name of the designated managing broker at the principal office
choice_c: The educational credentials of each designated managing broker
choice_d: Nothing, unless the Department specifically requests it
explanation: Section 5-45(b) requires the sponsoring broker to notify the Department of the name of all designated managing brokers and the office or offices each manages.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(b), in addition to naming a designated managing broker for each office, the sponsoring broker is responsible for:
choice_a: supervising all designated managing brokers
choice_b: personally handling every transaction in every office
choice_c: co-signing every listing agreement
choice_d: conducting the continuing education of all designated managing brokers
explanation: Section 5-45(b) states that the sponsoring broker names a designated managing broker for each office and is responsible for supervising all of the designated managing brokers.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), what must a sponsoring broker display on the outside of the physical office?
choice_a: An identification sign of adequate size and visibility
choice_b: The sponsoring broker's personal license certificate only
choice_c: A notarized copy of the office lease
choice_d: The Department's seal
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires the physical office to conspicuously display an identification sign of adequate size and visibility on the outside of the office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), except as otherwise provided, each sponsoring broker shall maintain, for the transaction of real estate business:
choice_a: an office, or place of business, within this State
choice_b: at least two offices, in different counties
choice_c: a virtual office only, with no physical location permitted
choice_d: an office staffed at all times by a licensed attorney
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires, except as otherwise provided in the Section, that each sponsoring broker maintain an office or place of business within Illinois for the transaction of real estate business.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), a physical record required to be maintained under the Act must be:
choice_a: securely stored and accessible for inspection by the Department at the sponsoring broker's principal office
choice_b: stored offsite at a Department-approved warehouse
choice_c: destroyed once the underlying transaction closes
choice_d: kept solely in the possession of the designated agent, not the office
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires a physical record to be securely stored and accessible for Department inspection at the sponsoring broker's principal office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), an electronic record required to be maintained under the Act must be:
choice_a: securely stored in the format in which it was originally generated, sent, or received, and accessible for inspection by the Department by secure electronic access
choice_b: printed and filed as a paper record within 30 days
choice_c: converted to a Department-mandated proprietary file format
choice_d: stored only on the individual licensee's personal device
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires electronic records to be securely stored in their originally generated, sent, or received format, and accessible to the Department by secure electronic access.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(e), to qualify for the exemption from maintaining a definite Illinois office, a nonresident broker must, among other conditions:
choice_a: maintain an active broker's license in the broker's other state of licensure
choice_b: have been licensed in Illinois at some point in the past
choice_c: maintain a bank account within Illinois
choice_d: obtain written consent from every Illinois sponsoring broker in the same county
explanation: Section 5-45(e)(1) requires the nonresident broker to maintain an active broker's license in the broker's other state of licensure as one condition of the office exemption.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(e), besides maintaining an active license in the other state, the nonresident broker office exemption also requires the broker to:
choice_a: maintain an office in the broker's other state of licensure
choice_b: visit Illinois in person at least once per quarter
choice_c: employ at least one Illinois-resident licensee
choice_d: maintain errors and omissions insurance issued by an Illinois carrier
explanation: Section 5-45(e)(2) requires the nonresident broker to maintain an office in the broker's other state of licensure as an additional condition of the exemption.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(e), the written statements a nonresident broker files appointing the Secretary as agent for service of process must be:
choice_a: in form and substance the same as those statements required under Section 5-60 of the Act, and shall operate to the same extent
choice_b: drafted independently, with no required consistency across sections
choice_c: filed only with the broker's home-state licensing authority
choice_d: renewed annually regardless of licensure status
explanation: Section 5-45(e) provides that the agent-for-service statements must be in the same form and substance as those required under Section 5-60, and operate to the same extent.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(b), besides directly handling earnest money, escrows, and contract negotiations, a designated managing broker's responsibilities also include:
choice_a: approval of all advertisements involving a licensee who has not completed his or her 45 hours of post-license education
choice_b: personally negotiating commission splits for every licensee in the office
choice_c: co-signing every brokerage agreement regardless of the agent's experience
choice_d: reviewing the office's marketing budget on a quarterly basis
explanation: Section 10-55(b) requires the designated managing broker to approve all advertisements involving a licensee who has not completed the 45 hours of post-license education.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(b), which advertisements must a designated managing broker approve?
choice_a: Advertisements involving any licensee who has not completed his or her 45 hours of post-license education
choice_b: All advertisements, regardless of any licensee's education status
choice_c: Only advertisements placed in print media
choice_d: Only advertisements for listings exceeding $500,000 in price
explanation: Section 10-55(b) ties the advertisement-approval duty specifically to advertisements involving licensees who have not yet completed the 45 hours of post-license education.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(a)(3), the official statement a managing broker applicant for endorsement must furnish from each state or jurisdiction of licensure must certify:
choice_a: that the managing broker has an active license, that the managing broker is in good standing, and any history of discipline against the managing broker in that state or jurisdiction
choice_b: only that the managing broker has passed the state's licensing exam
choice_c: only the managing broker's date of birth and Social Security number
choice_d: only that the managing broker has no outstanding tax liabilities
explanation: Section 5-60.5(a)(3) requires the official statement to certify active licensure, good standing, and any history of discipline against the managing broker in that state or jurisdiction.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(c), the managing broker's or broker's agreement to abide by the Act and submit to the Department's jurisdiction remains in force:
choice_a: for so long as the managing broker or broker is licensed by the State, and thereafter with respect to acts or omissions committed while licensed in the State
choice_b: only for the initial two-year licensing period
choice_c: only until the managing broker's home-state license expires
choice_d: only while the managing broker is actively practicing in Illinois
explanation: Section 5-60.5(c) provides that the agreement remains in force for as long as the managing broker or broker is licensed in Illinois, and continues thereafter for acts or omissions committed while licensed.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(f), upon receipt of any process or notice directed to a nonresident managing broker or broker, the Secretary shall:
choice_a: deliver a copy of the process or notice by regular mail or email to the mailing address or email address of record of the licensee
choice_b: personally travel to the licensee's other state to deliver notice
choice_c: publish notice in a newspaper of general circulation in Illinois
choice_d: forward the notice to the licensee's sponsoring broker only
explanation: Section 5-60.5(f) requires the Secretary, upon receiving process or notice, to deliver a copy by regular mail or email to the licensee's address of record.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Unlike the requirements for a broker's license by endorsement under Section 5-60.5(b), the managing broker endorsement requirements under Section 5-60.5(a) do not include:
choice_a: a requirement to complete 45 hours of post-license broker education based on fewer than 2 years of practice
choice_b: a test on Illinois-specific real estate brokerage laws
choice_c: an official statement from the applicant's other state or jurisdiction of licensure
choice_d: proof of successful completion of a Department-approved pre-license endorsement course
explanation: Section 5-60.5(b)(5) imposes a 45-hour post-license education requirement on broker endorsement applicants with less than 2 years of practice; Section 5-60.5(a) contains no equivalent provision for managing broker applicants, who must instead meet the separate 2-year active-practice threshold.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.1, a license granted under a reciprocal agreement prior to January 1, 2026:
choice_a: remains in force and may be renewed in the same manner as provided for a broker or managing broker license under Section 5-50 of the Act and by rule
choice_b: becomes void automatically on January 1, 2026
choice_c: must be reissued as a temporary permit pending a new exam
choice_d: may only be renewed once, with no further renewals permitted
explanation: Section 5-60.1 provides that licenses granted under reciprocal agreements before January 1, 2026 remain in force and may be renewed the same way as a broker or managing broker license under Section 5-50.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(16), it is a ground for discipline to:
choice_a: fail to account for or to remit any moneys or documents coming into the licensee's possession that belong to others
choice_b: decline to represent a customer who is not a client
choice_c: refer a transaction to another licensed brokerage
choice_d: charge a commission rate above the local market average
explanation: Section 20-20(16) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to account for or remit moneys or documents belonging to others that come into a licensee's possession.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(17), the special-account requirement applies to escrow moneys entrusted to a licensee while acting in which capacities?
choice_a: As a broker, escrow agent, or temporary custodian of the funds of others
choice_b: Only while acting as a broker; escrow agents are separately regulated
choice_c: Only while acting as a licensed attorney for a transaction
choice_d: Only when the licensee is a party to the transaction
explanation: Section 20-20(17) applies the special-account requirement to escrow moneys entrusted to a licensee while acting as a broker, escrow agent, or temporary custodian of the funds of others.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(19), a licensee is subject to discipline for failing to, upon request:
choice_a: furnish copies of documents relating to a real estate transaction to a party who has executed that document
choice_b: provide a written appraisal of the property
choice_c: disclose the licensee's personal income tax returns
choice_d: furnish a copy of the licensee's own personnel file
explanation: Section 20-20(19) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to furnish, upon request, copies of documents relating to a real estate transaction to a party who executed the document.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(20), it is a ground for discipline for a sponsoring broker or licensee to fail to:
choice_a: timely provide sponsorship or termination of sponsorship information to the Department
choice_b: timely pay local property taxes on brokerage-owned property
choice_c: timely renew the office's business insurance policy
choice_d: timely file the sponsoring broker's personal tax return
explanation: Section 20-20(20) makes it a ground for discipline for a sponsoring broker or licensee to fail to timely provide sponsorship or termination-of-sponsorship information to the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(22), it is a ground for discipline for a licensee to:
choice_a: commingle the money or property of others with the licensee's own money or property
choice_b: maintain more than one special account for the same office
choice_c: deposit personal funds into a special account to cover bank service charges, with the principals' written consent
choice_d: hold escrow funds in an interest-bearing account required by law
explanation: Section 20-20(22) makes commingling the money or property of others with the licensee's own money or property a ground for discipline.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(25.5), it is a ground for discipline to fail to have:
choice_a: a written brokerage agreement between the sponsoring broker and a client for whom the designated agent is working
choice_b: a written commission-splitting agreement between two cooperating brokers
choice_c: a notarized power of attorney for every transaction
choice_d: a written agreement between the designated agent and the buyer's lender
explanation: Section 20-20(25.5) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to have a written brokerage agreement between the sponsoring broker and a client for whom the designated agent is working.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(39), it is a ground for discipline to require a party to a transaction who is not a client of the licensee to:
choice_a: allow the licensee to retain a portion of the escrow moneys for payment of the licensee's commission or expenses as a condition for release of the escrow moneys to that party
choice_b: sign a written acknowledgment of the escrow account's location
choice_c: provide a forwarding address before the transaction closes
choice_d: obtain independent legal counsel before closing
explanation: Section 20-20(39) prohibits requiring a non-client party to allow the licensee to retain part of the escrow moneys for the licensee's commission or expenses as a condition of releasing the escrow moneys to that party.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(38), it is a ground for discipline to:
choice_a: pay or fail to disclose compensation in violation of Article 10 of the Act
choice_b: accept compensation directly from a title company for a routine title order
choice_c: advertise a commission rate that is lower than a competitor's
choice_d: decline to pay a referral fee to an unlicensed individual
explanation: Section 20-20(38) makes it a ground for discipline to pay or fail to disclose compensation in violation of Article 10 of the Act.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(27), apart from the 24-hour deadline that applies specifically to escrow records, a licensee who fails to provide information requested by the Department, or otherwise respond to that request, is subject to discipline if the failure continues beyond:
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 10 days
choice_c: 15 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: Section 20-20(27) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to provide information requested by the Department, or otherwise respond to that request, within 30 days of the request.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(a), the Department may impose a fine, for each violation of the Act's disciplinary grounds, not to exceed:
explanation: Section 20-20(a) authorizes the Department to impose a fine not to exceed $25,000 for each violation of the Act's disciplinary grounds.
